title: Promises without giving
odia:
ଦେବା ଦେବା କହୁଥିବା
ନାହିଁ ନଦେବା ନକରିବା।
literal_meaning: Keep saying that you will give, but neither give nor refuse. The two historical readings extend this mock instruction for as long as the moon and sun endure.
meaning_odia: ଦେବାର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ଦେଇ ଦେଉନଥିବା, ପୁଣି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ମନା ମଧ୍ୟ କରୁନଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ ଏହି ଢଗ କଟାକ୍ଷ କରେ। ଏଠାରେ ‘ନାହିଁ ନ କରିବା’ର ଅର୍ଥ ମନା ମଧ୍ୟ ନ କରିବା। ‘ଯାବଚ୍ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ଦିବାକର’—ଚନ୍ଦ୍ରସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଥିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ—ଏହି ଟାଳଟୁଳ ଯେପରି ଅନନ୍ତକାଳ ଚାଲିବ, ସେହି ଭାବକୁ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତିରେ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରିଛି। ଗୋପାଳ ଚନ୍ଦ୍ର ପ୍ରହରାଜଙ୍କ ସଂକଳିତ ଢଗ ଢମାଳି ବଚନର ପୃଷ୍ଠା ୧୦୦ର ପାଠ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତିରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୋଇଥିବାବେଳେ ପୃଷ୍ଠା ୧୦୬ର ପାଠ ଆଚରଣର ଅସଙ୍ଗତିକୁ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦକ୍ରମ ଭିନ୍ନ, କିନ୍ତୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗାତ୍ମକ ଅର୍ଥ ସମାନ। ମିଛ ଆଶାରେ ରଖିବା ଅପେକ୍ଷା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ମନା କରିଦେବା ଭଲ—ଏହା ଉକ୍ତିର ଆକ୍ଷରିକ ବକ୍ତବ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ, ତାହାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗରୁ ମିଳୁଥିବା ଶିକ୍ଷା।
explanation: The saying mocks someone who repeatedly promises to give, yet neither delivers nor clearly refuses. In Gopal Chandra Praharaj’s Dhaga Dhamali Bachana, the reading on printed page 100 begins with the promise; page 106 puts the failure to give or refuse first. Both carry the same satire. The moon-and-sun phrase exaggerates how endlessly the evasion can continue. A clear refusal is better than keeping someone waiting in false hope: that is the lesson drawn from the satire, not its literal instruction.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone repeatedly promises materials for a neighbour’s unfinished wall but provides none and never says no. The neighbour recalls this saying to expose the empty assurances.
cultural_context: The mock instruction imitates the promise-maker’s behaviour rather than endorsing it. The historical book explicitly labels the saying as satire. Its two versions reverse the order of the same clauses; the second brings the contradiction into focus before repeating the promise. The shorter uploaded wording remains above, while the two book readings are preserved separately below.

origin_note: The uploaded compilation and two readings in the separately identified 1926/n.1990 scan attest the saying. The historical gloss establishes its satirical target; these witnesses do not establish first composition or regional origin.
rights_note: Source quotations are excluded from the collection CC licence; no open licence for the compilations has been established. Translation, explanation and illustrative example are newly written Project Odisha commentary.
editorial_status: Interpretation revised 19 November 2026 using both visually checked historical readings and the user-approved explanation; uploaded wording retained. Publication status is recorded separately.

graphic.alt: A smiling man nods and raises his thumb as another person gestures beside an unfinished brick wall.
graphic.caption: An imagined promise of help leaves the neighbour waiting beside an unfinished wall.

odia_summary: ଦେବାକୁ କହି ନ ଦେବା ଓ ମନା ମଧ୍ୟ ନ କରିବା—ମିଛ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ପ୍ରତି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ।
english_summary: Satire of endless promises: neither giving nor clearly refusing.
